implementation_notes: Foundation's NotificationCenter is the process-wide channel: addObserver(forName:object:queue:using:) registers a block (or addObserver(_:selector:name:object:) a selector), post(name:object:userInfo:) publishes to every registered observer, and the returned token is handed to removeObserver to unsubscribe; a nil queue delivers on the posting thread, while .main guarantees main-actor delivery for UI subscribers. Newer Swift-flavoured APIs add typed messages and actor isolation, and publisher(for:) exposes the same notifications as a Combine publisher. It is the default for in-process, framework-level events.
pitfalls: userInfo is untyped ([AnyHashable: Any]), so a wrong key or type surfaces only inside the consumer.
Block observers must be removed; the registration does not disappear with the observer object, and a stale observer can crash the poster.
In Swift 6 concurrency the notification payload crosses actor boundaries: prefer the typed message APIs where available.

variants.name: Combine PassthroughSubject
variants.implementation_notes: Combine replaces the registry with a publisher: PassthroughSubject broadcasts elements to downstream subscribers, sending requires demand, and each subscriber holds an AnyCancellable whose deallocation cancels the subscription instead of an explicit removeObserver. Operators (map, filter, debounce, receive(on:)) transform the stream per subscriber, and CurrentValueSubject replays the latest value to new subscribers. The subject is a concrete Subject, so it can bridge imperative code into pipelines; note that Combine's availability is limited to Apple platforms.
pitfalls: A subscription dies when its AnyCancellable is deallocated - store the cancellable or the subscriber silently disappears.
PassthroughSubject has no replay and drops values when there are no subscribers or demand is zero; CurrentValueSubject is the alternative for late subscribers.
Combine is an Apple-platform framework (iOS 13/macOS 10.15 and later), so cross-platform server-side Swift needs NotificationCenter, AsyncSequence or a NIO-based channel instead.
